topics.title: Did Plague Just Kill Someone in Siberia?
topics.hook: A plague lab worker died in Siberia. 200 people were put under watch. Here's what's actually true.
facts: 28-year-old lab technician at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute: hospitalised Sep 29, died Oct 2 (per a friend to CNN); official diagnosis 'pneumonia of unknown aetiology'
Nearly 200 people placed under medical observation (CNBC, Oct 5)
Oct 10: WHO says NO plague case registered; tests on her and her contacts negative, cause still unknown
Plague is a bacterium (Yersinia pestis), not a virus; untreated pneumonic plague can kill in 18–24 h, but common antibiotics cure it early (WHO)
topics.risk: High care: say 'suspected', end on the WHO update, never name or show the victim, no lab-leak/bioweapon speculation.

topics.title: This Year's Nobel: They Control Neurons With Light
topics.hook: A protein from pond algae won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
facts: 2026 Medicine Nobel: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel, 'for light-gated ion channels and optogenetics' (Oct 5)
Channelrhodopsin came from a single-celled alga; it became a light switch for nerve cells
topics.risk: Low. Call it a research tool; don't claim it already cures diseases in people.

topics.title: A Nobel Prize for a Telescope Buried in Ice
topics.hook: The 2026 Physics Nobel went to a detector frozen inside Antarctica.
facts: 2026 Physics Nobel: Francis Halzen, for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (Oct 6)
IceCube is a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice fitted with light sensors that catch 'ghost particles'
topics.risk: Low. Check licence before using IceCube/NSF photos.

topics.title: A Dead Star May Have Given Birth to a New Planet
topics.hook: Hubble had this clue for 25 years. Nobody noticed.
facts: White dwarf HS 0209+0832: odd chemical signatures sat in Hubble's archive for 25+ years
High niobium levels point to a possible 'second-generation planet', the first candidate of its kind (Nature Astronomy)
topics.risk: Low. Say 'may' / 'candidate'. ESA/Hubble art is CC BY 4.0 (credit it).

topics.title: You Can See Halley's Comet This Month (Sort Of)
topics.hook: Halley's Comet won't return until 2061, but pieces of it hit our sky this month.
facts: Orionid meteor shower peaks the night of Oct 21 into Oct 22; it's debris from Halley's Comet (NASA)
Meteors enter at ~41 miles/s; 10–20 per hour in ideal skies; Halley last seen 1986, next 2061 (BBC Weather)
topics.why_now: Peak Oct 21–22, 2026: must post before Oct 20
topics.risk: Low. Time-sensitive.

topics.title: Why Plane Windows Are Never Square
topics.hook: Square corners tore jets apart in the sky.
facts: The de Havilland Comet, the first jet airliner, entered service in 1952
Jan 1954: BOAC Flight 781 broke up off Elba, all 35 killed
Cause: metal fatigue at stress points around square cut-outs; redesign used rounded openings
topics.risk: Say 'square openings/cut-outs': the crack began at an antenna window, not a passenger window.

topics.title: On Venus, a Day Is Longer Than a Year
topics.hook: On Venus, your birthday comes before tomorrow.
facts: A Venus day is 243 Earth days; its year is 225 Earth days
Venus spins backward, so the Sun rises in the west
topics.risk: Low.

topics.title: The Day the Sun Set Telegraphs on Fire
topics.hook: In 1859, the Sun made telegraph wires spark and shock their operators.
facts: Sept 1859 Carrington Event: telegraph stations sparked and caught fire; operators got shocks
Auroras seen as far south as Cuba, Hawaii and southern Japan
A storm that size today could cause blackouts and damage satellites
topics.why_now: Evergreen (the Sun is near solar maximum)
topics.risk: Low. Avoid 'it will destroy the internet' hype.

topics.title: The 72-Second Signal From Space Nobody Explained
topics.hook: In 1977, a telescope caught a signal so strange the scientist wrote 'Wow!'
facts: Aug 15, 1977, Big Ear radio telescope, Ohio; Jerry Ehman circled it and wrote 'Wow!'
Lasted the full 72-second window; never detected again
topics.risk: Low. Say 'still unexplained', don't claim aliens.

topics.title: Russia Dug the Deepest Hole on Earth. Then Stopped
topics.hook: The deepest hole humans ever dug is just 23 cm wide.
facts: Kola Superdeep Borehole reached 12,262 m in 1989, the deepest artificial point on Earth
The hole is only 23 cm (9 in) wide
Drilling stopped in 1992: rock at 180 °C, far hotter than expected
topics.why_now: Evergreen (ties into the Russia news week)
topics.risk: Skip the 'sounds of hell' hoax, or debunk it as the twist.

topics.title: MH370: The Plane That Vanished
topics.hook: 239 people. A Boeing 777. And it simply vanished.
facts: Disappeared from radar on 8 March 2014, Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, 227 passengers + 12 crew
Satellite 'handshakes' showed it flew far south over the southern Indian Ocean
Debris confirmed from the plane washed ashore in the western Indian Ocean in 2015–16
Official search of 120,000 km² suspended Jan 2017; cause still undetermined

sources.label: Reuters · Jun 29, 2026 (search extended; snippet only, not opened)

topics.why_now: Ocean Infinity's 2025–26 search ended Jan 2026 with no find; Malaysia reportedly extended the deal Jun 2026 (unverified, snippet)
topics.risk: Families still grieving: no pilot-blame claims, attribute every theory.

topics.title: Apollo 13: 'Houston, We've Had a Problem'
topics.hook: 200,000 miles from home, their spaceship exploded.
facts: April 1970: an oxygen tank exploded two days into the mission; the Moon landing was aborted
The lunar module became a lifeboat for three men for four days: cold, wet, short of water
Crew and Mission Control improvised a fix to make square CO₂ filters work in a round socket
Cause: a routine stir ignited damaged wire insulation inside an oxygen tank
topics.why_now: Artemis II flew around the Moon in April 2026: the first crew past the Moon since Apollo
topics.risk: Low. NASA media is public domain. '200,000 miles' in the hook is approximate: check.

topics.title: Chernobyl: The Night Reactor 4 Exploded
topics.hook: A safety test caused the worst nuclear disaster in history.
facts: 26 April 1986, during a safety test at reactor No. 4 near Pripyat, Soviet Ukraine
~49,000 evacuated within 36 h; zone later widened to 30 km (~68,000 more)
The USSR admitted it only after radiation alarms went off in Sweden
134 workers had acute radiation syndrome; 28 died within three months
topics.risk: Long-term death toll is disputed (UN up to 4,000 vs 16,000 across Europe): quote both.

topics.title: Concorde: Why the Fastest Jet Died
topics.hook: You could fly London to New York in 3.5 hours. In 1976.
facts: Entered service 21 January 1976 (Air France + British Airways); only 20 built
Supersonic flight more than halved travel times, but sonic booms limited it to over-ocean routes
25 July 2000: Air France Flight 4590 crash, its only fatal accident
Retired in 2003, 27 years after service began
topics.why_now: 50 years of Concorde service (Jan 21, 1976 → 2026); new supersonic jets in development
topics.risk: '3.5 hours' is the commonly cited time: unverified, check before scripting.

topics.title: Tenerife: Two Jumbo Jets, One Runway
topics.hook: The deadliest air disaster ever happened on the ground.
facts: 27 March 1977: KLM and Pan Am 747s collided on a fog-covered runway at Los Rodeos, Tenerife
583 people died, the deadliest accident in aviation history
The KLM jet began its take-off run in dense fog while the Pan Am jet was still on the runway
It reshaped cockpit teamwork and standard radio phrases (widely reported; unverified here)
topics.risk: Medium: respectful tone, no wreckage gore; animation only.

topics.title: The Explosion That Flattened 80 Million Trees
topics.hook: In 1908, something exploded over Siberia with the power of 1,000 atomic bombs.
facts: 30 June 1908, Tunguska, Siberia: an air burst flattened about 2,150 km² of forest (an estimated 80 million trees, unverified figure)
Likely a 50–60 m space rock exploding 5–10 km up
Estimated 10–15 megatons of TNT; no impact crater ever confirmed
topics.risk: '1,000 atomic bombs' is an approximation (~1,000× Hiroshima): unverified framing, keep it 'about'.

topics.title: The Jet That Ran Out of Fuel Because of Maths
topics.hook: A metric mix-up turned a Boeing 767 into a glider.
facts: 23 July 1983: Air Canada Flight 143, a Boeing 767, ran out of fuel midway, Montreal to Edmonton
A pounds-vs-kilograms conversion error left it with 45% of the fuel it needed
The crew glided it from 41,000 ft to a former air force base (by then a racetrack) at Gimli; no serious injuries
topics.risk: Low.

topics.title: The Year Without a Summer
topics.hook: In 1816, it snowed in June. A volcano did it.
facts: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora, Indonesia: the largest in at least 1,300 years
Global temperatures fell 0.4–0.7 °C; Europe's coldest summer on record 1766–2000
Crop failures and food shortages across the Northern Hemisphere
topics.risk: Hook 'snowed in June' (New England, 1816) and the Frankenstein link are popular framing: unverified, check before scripting.

topics.title: A 2,000-Year-Old Computer Found in a Shipwreck
topics.hook: Divers found a computer from ancient Greece.
facts: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a shipwreck off a Greek island in 1901
A hand-powered gear model of the solar system that predicted eclipses decades ahead
The oldest known example of an analogue computer
topics.risk: Low. Dating (2nd–1st century BC) is debated: say 'over 2,000 years old'.

topics.title: All Four Engines Stopped. Then the Captain Spoke
topics.hook: 'Ladies and gentlemen, we have a small problem. All four engines have stopped.'
facts: 24 June 1982: British Airways Flight 9, a 747, flew into volcanic ash over Indonesia
All four engines flamed out; it glided for minutes
It glided out of the ash, all engines restarted (one later shut down), and it landed safely in Jakarta
topics.risk: Low. Quote wording varies slightly between sources: verify before scripting.

topics.title: The Man Who Survived an Iron Rod Through His Head
topics.hook: An iron bar shot through his skull. He survived.
facts: 1848: railroad foreman Phineas Gage had an iron tamping rod driven completely through his head, through the left frontal lobe
He lived 12 more years; friends said he was 'no longer Gage'
A founding case for how the brain shapes personality
topics.risk: Medium: no gore; illustrate with a skull diagram. Personality-change stories are exaggerated in pop retellings.

topics.title: The Largest Living Thing Is a Forest of One Tree
topics.hook: This whole forest is one single organism.
facts: Pando: a quaking aspen clone in Utah, ~47,000 'trees' that are genetically one tree sharing one root system
Its roots span 42.8 hectares (106 acres)
Generally held to be the world's largest single organism by weight
topics.risk: Age estimates vary widely: avoid a single number.
